fixes.explanation: That's the news, baker. In the twelfth year of the exile, on the fifth day of the tenth month, a fugitive from Jerusalem comes to Ezekiel and reports, "The city has been taken!" (Ezekiel 33:21). Ezekiel is the prophet telling this. That's a short sentence, and I think it landed like a dropped tray of cookies.

Peace would be a nice headline, friend, but that's not what the man brings. He reports, "The city has been taken!" (Ezekiel 33:21). This verse says nothing about the king. The man who escaped from Jerusalem comes with that one sentence.

I wish that were the report, baker. But the man who escaped from Jerusalem says, "The city has been taken!" (Ezekiel 33:21). That news is about the city, and the verse doesn't mention the walls. I think it's the kind of news that's hard to carry.

Mouth it is! The evening before the man arrives, the hand of the LORD is upon Ezekiel (Ezekiel 33:22). The text says He opened Ezekiel's mouth before the man came in the morning. Ezekiel is no longer mute.

Good guess, friend, but eyes aren't what the text names. It says the LORD "opened my mouth before the man came to me in the morning." (Ezekiel 33:22). So the verse is about his mouth. Ezekiel says, "I was no longer mute." (Ezekiel 33:22).

Ears make sense, baker, since a prophet has to listen. But the text says the hand of the LORD was upon Ezekiel and "…He opened my mouth…" (Ezekiel 33:22). That was before the man came to him in the morning. Ezekiel was mute, and then he wasn't.

I get why you'd think so, baker, since the city was just reported taken. But God asks something else. After listing the blood, the idols and the shed blood, He says, "Should you then possess the land?" (Ezekiel 33:25). The question is about the land, not the walls.

Yes, friend. God says those in the strongholds and caves "…will die by plague." (Ezekiel 33:27). Sword for the ruins, wild animals for the open field, plague for the strongholds and caves. This is a heavy part.

Being taken captive is a fair guess, friend, but it's not what God says here. He says those in the strongholds and caves "…will die by plague." (Ezekiel 33:27). The sword, the wild animals and the plague are all in that verse. I think this one hurts.

This one is true, friend. God says, "The mountains of Israel will become desolate, so that no one will pass through." (Ezekiel 33:28). In the same verse He says He will make the land a desolate waste. This is a heavy line.

Nope, friend, that's not what they say. God says each one tells his brother, "Come and hear the message that has come from the LORD!" (Ezekiel 33:30). They say it near the city walls and in the doorways of their houses. Those words are an invitation to come and hear.

Right, baker. God says, "Although they express love with their mouths, their hearts pursue dishonest gain." (Ezekiel 33:31). Their mouths say one thing and their hearts chase another. It's like someone who says "love you!" with a big smile while quietly reaching for your wallet.

That's the one, baker. God says Ezekiel is to them "…like a singer of love songs with a beautiful voice, who skillfully plays an instrument." (Ezekiel 33:32). The verse also says they hear his words but do not put them into practice. That's the part that matters.
